patches.why: digitization defect, not Migne's plate: Corpus Corporum metathesized the h and the l. The Google scan clips line-initial characters down the lower left column of p. 368, so the word survives on the plate as 'hthali. »' — but the surviving letters are decisive, h-t-h-a-l-i, and '-hthali' cannot yield the TEI's '-htlali'. Read at 450 dpi and again at 900 dpi. The gloss's own etymology (Latitudo, Jerome's interpretation of Nephthali) corroborates it. Same class as 8968's 'significaRuth'.
